subject_line: Cook Once, Eat All Week on Carnivore
opening: Hey, it's Chloe. This week's issue is packed: a batch-cooking plan that takes one afternoon and covers five days of meals, plus some real talk about what happens to your body in week one. We've also got something for anyone hosting Thanksgiving while eating carnivore, because that situation is its own adventure. Let's get into it.

hero.title: Carnivore Meal Prep: One Afternoon, Five Days of Food
hero.teaser: Most people fall off carnivore not because the diet is hard, but because they're standing in the kitchen at 7pm with nothing ready. Marcus put together a batch-cooking plan that fits into one afternoon and keeps you fed, with portions already sized for weight loss, all the way through the week. The sequence matters more than you'd think. See the protocol before your next grocery run.

supporting.title: Hosting Thanksgiving at 60 When You Eat Carnivore
supporting.teaser: Chloe found a way to host twelve people without cooking two separate dinners, and the trick is simpler than you'd expect.

supporting.title: Peeing All Night on Carnivore? Why Week One Does It
supporting.teaser: Sarah explains what's actually happening in your body during week one, and at what point you can stop setting your alarm for 3am.

supporting.title: Fatty Liver After 50: What Carnivore Changes
supporting.teaser: Your doctor said lose weight, but Sarah goes deeper into what cutting carbs actually does to liver fat, and the answer isn't what most people expect.

community_pulse.question: I've been eating carnivore for a couple of weeks now and I'm still waking up two or three times a night to pee. Is something wrong with me?
community_pulse.answer: Nothing's wrong. Many people find that the first week or two brings a noticeable increase in bathroom trips, especially at night. It's your body releasing stored water as glycogen drops. Sarah's piece this week, 'Peeing All Night on Carnivore? Why Week One Does It,' walks through exactly when this tends to settle down.

community_pulse.question: I want to tell my friends about carnivore because it's helped me so much, but I don't know how to bring it up without sounding preachy. Anyone else feel this way?
community_pulse.answer: This one comes up a lot in our community. Many people find that leading with their own results, without prescribing anything, keeps the conversation relaxed and curious rather than defensive. A short, honest 'here's what changed for me' tends to land better than any amount of explaining the science.

community_pulse.question: Keto stopped working for me after a couple of years. My weight crept back and my energy tanked. Is carnivore actually different, or will the same thing happen?
community_pulse.answer: It's a fair question, and the honest answer is that it depends on what caused the stall. Many people find that going full carnivore removes the food variables that quietly slow progress on broader keto, things like hidden carbs or snacking on foods that feel compliant but aren't. Protein satiety tends to be stronger too, which makes sticking to it easier over time.

try_this_week: Pick one cook-once anchor protein this week. Before you go grocery shopping, choose a single large cut, a brisket, a pork shoulder, a whole chicken, that you'll cook in bulk and portion out. Even one anchor protein ready in the fridge removes the 'nothing to eat' moment that derails most people. That's the first move in Marcus's prep plan, and it works on its own even if you don't do the rest yet.
looking_ahead: Next week we're getting into something a lot of you have asked about: what your blood work is actually supposed to look like after 90 days on carnivore, and which numbers your doctor might flag that aren't actually a problem.
